instruction:
A directory-service implementer is checking whether a replacement Unicode library preserves the LDAP caseIgnoreSubstringsMatch behavior. Produce a diagnostic table for the six fixtures below using RFC 4517's matching rule and RFC 4518's preparation, with RFC Editor verified errata as of 2026-09-19. Follow the profile's referenced stringprep tables. For this compatibility check, Unicode 3.2.0 normalization is version-locked to its original decomposition mappings: do not apply normalization corrections first introduced in later Unicode versions. This last requirement also applies if a modern library silently supplies a corrected mapping.

Each operand is a sequence of Unicode scalar values, written in hexadecimal U+ notation; spaces BETWEEN tokens are notation only. An actual space occurs only where U+0020 appears. There is exactly one initial, one any, and one final substring in each assertion, in that order. These are direct matching-rule test inputs, not textual LDAP filters. All input strings use Unicode Directory String syntax. Do not apply a server's separate storage-admission policy before this matching-rule diagnostic.

Prepare the attribute value and each of the three assertion components independently all the way through the specified preparation process. If preparation of an operand fails, report FAIL for that operand; still report the independently prepared other operands. Then evaluate the matching rule, including failure and the required relationship between substring regions. Do not substitute a generic stringprep profile, substring search, current Unicode casefold, or a library's final Boolean for the specified diagnostic computation.

Input table:
case | attribute | initial | any | final
T1 | U+0020 U+03D2 U+00AD U+0020 U+212A U+0020 U+0041 U+0020 | U+03C5 U+0020 | U+006B U+0020 | U+0061
T2 | U+0061 U+0020 U+0301 U+0062 U+0020 U+0063 | U+0061 | U+0020 U+0301 U+0062 | U+0063
T3 | U+0066 U+006F U+006F U+0020 U+0062 U+0061 U+0072 | U+0066 U+006F U+006F U+0020 | U+0020 | U+0020 U+0062 U+0061 U+0072
T4 | U+0041 U+FE0F U+0009 U+004B U+0020 U+0042 | U+0041 U+0020 | U+004B U+0020 | U+0042
T5 | U+0061 U+1D2C U+0062 U+0020 U+0063 | U+0061 | U+1D2C U+0062 | U+0063
T6 | U+2F868 U+0020 U+03D2 U+0020 U+212A | U+2136A U+0020 | U+03C5 U+0020 | U+006B

Return only a table, T1 through T6 in order:
case | attribute_prepared | initial_prepared | any_prepared | final_prepared | result
Represent every prepared operand as its complete sequence of U+ hexadecimal code points, including every leading, internal and trailing space. Use FAIL only for preparation failure and EMPTY only for a successfully prepared empty sequence. Use TRUE, FALSE or UNDEFINED for the matching-rule result. Do not omit a row.
output_format: case | attribute_prepared | initial_prepared | any_prepared | final_prepared | result
